correctness.rationale: Every normalized molecule is in the convex hull of finite directed edge molecules in a unit-edge graph; the explicit rank-two operator has norm exactly one because edge ab maps to δ_c−δ_b/2 (norm one by a transport plan and a 1-Lipschitz witness) and all other edge molecules have image norm <=1/2. For every norming edge functional the reverse evaluation has magnitude <=1/2; molecular face convexity extends this to all norming pairs, while edge bc attains 1/2. For an arbitrary norm-one operator S, choose a norming edge and an extreme dual norming its image. An extreme unit Lipschitz potential must have a connected tight-edge graph and integral values. At the chosen edge the increment is ±1 (direct radius witness) or 0; in the latter case the auxiliary edge weights w=2−|Δf| give a shortest-path potential h with |Δh|=2 on the flat edge and |Δh|<=w elsewhere. The two norm-one potentials (f±h)/2 norm that molecule up to signs and sum to f, forcing 1<=2v(S). No asymptotic or nonstandard unverified lemma is needed. Exact script artifacts/verify.py ran successfully over all 770 connected labeled graphs of orders 3–5, including 541 with triangles; the infinite class rests on the proof, not on the enumeration. Lower and upper equality domain, basepoint, complex exclusion and weighted limits were rechecked.

value.rationale: This gives a complete exact index for every finite connected unit-edge graph containing a triangle, including arbitrarily large non-equilateral and irregular metrics, rather than isolated 3- or 5-point values. It supplies a structural obstruction in terms of the presence of a minimal metric equilateral triple and a uniform rank-two operator usable for all graph sizes. The graph index-one parity theorem and the universal graph one-half lower estimate left this natural nonbipartite class unclassified. The result cannot be deduced just from containing a three-point equilateral free subspace, because numerical index is not monotone under arbitrary inclusions. The theorem is motivated by a natural local graph feature with a sharp global operator consequence, not a routine small-parameter recomputation.
